expectations.text: The game is run headless with --headless and a bounded run such as --quit-after <frames>, so the command terminates on its own
expectations.evidence: Response shows the exact command: 'godot --headless --path /tmp/eval-work/smoke-w --quit-after 120' with explanation '120 process frames (~2 seconds at 60 FPS). Long enough for _ready to run on the full main scene tree; short enough not to hang.'

expectations.text: Both the process exit code and the captured output are checked, including scanning for SCRIPT ERROR / ERROR: / Parse Error lines rather than trusting exit code 0 alone
expectations.evidence: Response provides a one-liner that explicitly checks both: '[ $exit_code -eq 0 ]' for exit code, and 'echo "$output" | grep -qE "SCRIPT ERROR|ERROR:|Parse Error"' for error lines in output. Narrative also explains 'Godot can exit 0 even when a script error occurred, so you must scan output explicitly.'
